answers.answer: Reveal the top region card and place the King there. Each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Of their ten Caballeros, two go in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal a region card for the King; each player takes another for home. Ten: two home, one success track, seven court.

answers.answer: In round 1 the players choose who starts. In later rounds the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts; others play clockwise. A power-card value already played that round cannot be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: round 1 chosen starter; later, last player from prior round begins; others clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are in descending power-card value. At the start of their turn, a player recruits up to the Caballero allowance pictured on their power card, then chooses an available action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Take turns in descending power-card value’; ‘At the start of your turn recruit up to’ the allowance; action card follows recruitment.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the recruitment difference. The King's region and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: take your own from the board to make up the difference; King's region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves up to the action card's number from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, and may be divided freely among those destinations. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: ‘maximum’; move from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo, ‘dividing the allowance freely.’

answers.answer: Yes. Deployment and special action may be done in either order, but each activity must be completed before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Do them in either order’; neither may be split or interleaved; may decline special action.

answers.answer: After a player's turn, their selected card is laid aside and later players cannot choose it. After all players have taken a turn, remaining face-up cards are discarded. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure steps 4–5: selected card laid aside; discard remaining face-up cards after all turns; King card revealed again and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected; the King-moving actions are the exception to the taboo rule.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: King's region is taboo for Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard movement; it may still be scored; moving the King changes the protected region.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. Any or all may enter regardless of the King's location. They cannot be removed by an action and leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘Announce clearly how many’; any or all may go into Castillo regardless of King's location; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: After rounds 3, 6, and 9, choose destinations secretly before uncovering the Castillo: each player sets a disk to one board region other than the King's region, and all of that player's Castillo pieces go to that one region. Then score the Castillo; reveal disks and move the pieces to selected destinations (replace Castillo empty); finally score the nine regions in scoring-track order.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages 1–4: secretly select before uncovering; score Castillo; reveal and empty Castillo; score nine regions. Timing is after rounds 3, 6, 9.

answers.answer: No: all of a player's Castillo Caballeros go to one region; the King's region is prohibited; and none may be retained in Castillo. If the King’s region was illegally selected, those pieces go to that player's court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring: all pieces must go to one region; King's region prohibited; Castillo emptied; illegally selected King's region sends pieces to court.

answers.answer: The three players tied for most each score 3 points (second-place value); the player with three Caballeros scores 1 point. Grandes do not count as Caballeros and contribute zero to majority.
answers.evidence: Example: 5/3/1 counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1. Grande marks home and contributes zero Caballeros.

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6; the player with 3 scores 4; both players with 2 score 0.
answers.evidence: Example on 6/4/2: counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In two-player games only first place can pay; in three-player games first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first drops to second-place value, which is outside the two-player payable ranks, so both score zero.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first; three players first and second. Apply player-count cutoff after tie shift; two-player tie for first pays neither.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including during special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King's region gets +2, and the sole majority holder with their own Grande in a region gets +2. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever relevant region is scored, including special scorings: King's +2; home +2; neither on tie for first.

answers.answer: No. Specially scoring Castillo reveals and scores its contents, then covers them again over the same Caballeros. They are not redistributed; they wait for general scoring.
answers.evidence: Special scoring of Castillo: score it and cover the same pieces again; redistribution waits until general scoring.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region, cannot be stacked on the other scoreboard, and cannot be reversed or rotated to change values.
answers.evidence: Mobile scoreboard: Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King's region; cannot stack; place right side up, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: You may move your Grande to another region except the King's region or Castillo. It cannot leave the King's region. The destination may already contain several Grandes; it becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Grande: move to another region except King's region or Castillo; cannot leave King's region; destination may have several Grandes; becomes new home region.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which card you choose, though taking the visible top card is apparent.
answers.evidence: Power Cards: return any one played power card, including this turn's; need not reveal which.

answers.answer: The game ends after the third general scoring, after round 9 and after all its stages. The player furthest along the success track wins; no additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: finish all stages of third general scoring after round 9; furthest along success track wins; no additional tiebreaker.

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: separate and shuffle each stack; Turn Structure: reveal top card of each five stacks; standard round marker starts at 1.

answers.answer: No. Played cards remain in each player's face-up used stack, with only the top card visible; they do not return to hand unless recovered by a special action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: played cards remain in face-up used stack with only top visible; a special action can recover a played card.

answers.answer: If you move the King before ordinary deployment, his new position determines adjacent destinations. The King card may place him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment uses King's new position if moved before deployment; King card puts King in any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: Keep Veto before you after taking it. It can stop one special action during this round or the next, but cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Veto: put card before you and retain it; stop one special action this or next round; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: While Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as a player starts: an announced action can be stopped before execution, or the remaining part of an incomplete special action can be prevented. A completed action cannot be vetoed, and executed parts are not undone.
answers.evidence: Veto: announce before executing; object as soon as player starts; may stop before execution or prevent remaining incomplete part; completed actions cannot be vetoed; executed parts not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: discard after using once; if unused, discard at end of next round.

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; a player with an empty court sends none. The selecting player is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends all two to the provinces. The selecting player is unaffected and keeps their five.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — three from court: each fellow player sends three or all if fewer; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed paragraph and card face require each player, including the selector, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Begin with the player to the selector's left, proceed clockwise, and the selector goes last. Pieces may come from any regions and/or court, never the King's region or Castillo. The source gives no shortfall rule if a player has fewer than three eligible pieces. The bold heading says ‘fellow players,’ conflicting with the detailed paragraph and card face.
answers.evidence: The King returns: detailed execution and card say each player, including selector, sends three; left then clockwise, selector last; sources any regions/court except King's region/Castillo; no shortfall rule. Heading says ‘fellow players.’

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner's provinces. No pieces may be taken from courts, the King's region, or Castillo. The source does not give a fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selector chooses one from a region for each player including themselves; excludes courts, King's region and Castillo; no explicit fallback for no eligible piece.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. A player with a legal region containing at least two of their Caballeros must choose a region containing at least two, then return two to the provinces. The summary does not explicitly state that choice constraint as a separate rule, but says the disk choice must contain at least two; the source gap concerns protected-region-only cases.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: each chooses a region on disk, simultaneous and revealed together; it must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros; return two.

answers.answer: Choose a region with one of their Caballeros and return that one to the provinces. This singleton fallback applies when the player has at most one in every region.
answers.evidence: The stated singleton fallback applies if player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects a region with at least one of their Caballeros on their disk; choices are revealed together, and they return all their own pieces in that region to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all: simultaneous secret disk selection; region with at least one; return all own there; player with none in any region unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, choose any region including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; they are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Pick one region: any region including King's region or Castillo; normal rules, rank limits and bonuses; Castillo contents covered again without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is determined by the current first scoreboard value. Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify; Granada with 4/0/0 does qualify. Applicable home and King's bonuses apply to special scorings.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions: current first value 4; Galicia 8/4/0 removes it, Granada 4/0/0 adds it; special scoring bonuses apply.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country, Aragon, and Valencia; the printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile, New Castile, and Granada. Current first scoreboard values determine group eligibility, so mobile scoreboards can remove/add regions. Castillo is not scored in all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: all-5 printed group and Castillo excluded; all-6/7 printed group; categories use current first value.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; ties for first score nothing because they would ordinarily receive second-place value. Other ranks score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First position only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing; other ranks get nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Both board regions tied for the most are scored. Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Most Caballeros: score all regions tied for most; Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Least Caballeros: compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo excluded.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly chooses another region with their disk, and choices are revealed simultaneously. A player choosing the King's region or the region being vacated sends their pieces to their court instead. The taboo prevents taking pieces out of the King's region, and Castillo cannot be emptied with this card.
answers.evidence: Movement: all fellow players move all own pieces out; secret simultaneous destinations; choosing King's or vacated region sends pieces to court; Castillo cannot be emptied.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, at most one region away. The King card can place him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one away; King card: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to your court. This is separate from the 4-stack card's ordinary deployment of up to four from court to board; either complete activity may go first. The source gives no shortfall procedure if provinces cannot supply both.
answers.evidence: The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four court-to-board deployment, either activity first; no shortfall procedure.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose on disks and reveal simultaneously. The disk allows the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo. Score each uniquely chosen region normally; a region chosen by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: Each secretly chooses a region: secret disks, reveal simultaneously; nine regions including King's but not Castillo; unique choices score, duplicates do not.

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other non-King regions and/or Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue all-own-from-one-region: distribute among other regions and/or Castillo, may return some to original; origins exclude King's and Castillo, destinations exclude King's.

answers.answer: Up to two additional own Caballeros may come from court; with the normal up-to-one deployment, up to three may enter the board. Only the normal one requires adjacency; the two additional pieces may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two more from court: up to two additional to any non-King regions/Castillo; normal one makes up to three, only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one special alternative, not both. Normal deployment of up to one still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Up to five Caballeros may be own and/or foreign, but they must come from one origin region. They may be distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue up to five: own and/or foreign from one origin region to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three other players' Caballeros, from one or multiple non-King board regions; your own pieces cannot be included. They may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo is never a source.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any three foreign: up to three other players' from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three card allows up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. The any-four card allows up to four own and/or foreign from any non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo is not a source; the four-piece card's specified destination wording is ‘other regions.’
answers.evidence: Intrigue table: any three allows any non-King origins to any non-King destinations/Castillo; any four allows own/foreign into other non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. Multiple origins are allowed. Origins may be any regions, but the summary's general rules prohibit removing from King's region or Castillo; destinations may be non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue: ‘two own and two foreign’ means up to two own plus two foreign, separate allowances, from any regions; all entries subject to taboo and Castillo rules.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo cannot be a source; the King's region is taboo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any four of your own: up to four own only, from any non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; general Castillo rules apply.

answers.answer: On the 4-stack secret-choice scoring card, a player may select the King's region but not Castillo; duplicated choices are not scored. By contrast, the card that lets its player choose one location may choose any region, including both the King's region and Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: nine regions including King's, not Castillo; Stack 2 pick one region: any region including King's or Castillo.

answers.answer: The mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The place-or-move action can introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup: place both mobile scoreboards beside board. Mobile scoreboard action: introduce one from beside board or move one already on board to different region.

answers.answer: Each player receives thirteen power cards in their own color, values 1–13. Each card shows a recruitment allowance of 0–6 Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Components/setup: 65 power cards, values 1–13 per color; give each player their color's thirteen power cards.
